title: How Should a Home Robot Update Its Memories When Human Routines Change?
abstract: arXiv:2611.29818v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A home robot that helps with chores needs to know where objects are, but people move objects according to routines that change and later change back. The robot's memory must adapt to the new routine without erasing experience that may become useful again. One approach is to have a language model maintain written summaries of the home from the robot's own observations, but existing evaluations of such memories use static worlds. We explore simulated households where a resident gets sick, recovers, and later gets sick again. We compare a rule that keeps every room an object has been seen in, language-model memories that store only written summaries, and language-model memories that can also read the raw history of sightings. The rule outperforms every summary-only memory, and giving language models the sighting history closes the gap. Surprisingly, writing summaries on top of the history adds nothing we can measure. translated_title: 当人类日常习惯发生变化时，家用机器人应如何更新其记忆？
translated_abstract: 一个帮助做家务的家用机器人需要知道物品的位置，但人们会根据日常习惯移动物品，而这些习惯会改变，之后又会变回来。机器人的记忆必须适应新的习惯，同时不能抹掉将来可能再次有用的经验。一种方法是让语言模型根据机器人自身的观察来维护关于家庭环境的书面摘要，但目前对这类记忆的评估都使用静态环境。我们探索了模拟家庭场景，其中住户生病、康复、之后又再次生病。我们比较了三种方法：保留物品出现过的每个房间的规则方法、仅存储书面摘要的语言模型记忆、以及还能读取原始目击历史记录的语言模型记忆。结果表明，规则方法优于所有仅存储摘要的记忆，而让语言模型访问目击历史则可以弥补这一差距。令人惊讶的是，在历史记录之上再生成摘要并未带来任何可测量的增益。当疾病再次……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过模拟住户“生病—康复—再生病”的动态家庭场景，发现简单的“记录物品出现过的所有房间”规则优于仅存储书面摘要的语言模型记忆，而让语言模型读取原始目击历史可弥补差距，且在历史之上再生成摘要并无额外收益。
en_tdlr: In simulated households where a resident's routine shifts (getting sick, recovering, then getting sick again), a simple rule of remembering every room an object was seen in outperforms summary-only language-model memories, and giving language models access to the raw sighting history closes the gap—writing summaries on top of the history adds no measurable benefit.
